script: I can't believe they ruined my favorite dessert—this changed everything!. I was halfway through my morning smoothie—frozen strawberries, banana, a splash of almond milk—when I remembered I'd just brushed my teeth. The taste hit me like orange juice on fresh enamel. It was brutal, bruh. (I know, right?) I swear, fruit and chocolate are like that same combo, just a different level of gross. Then I tried chocolate‑strawberry, like, seriously? The "ew" was instant. And crepes? Don't even. Tossing fruit on them turns the whole thing into a soggy, tasteless mess. Same with tres leches; the fruit just drags the flavor down. I can handle berries or vanilla on their own, and I even love vanilla‑chocolate together. But fruit‑dessert mashups? That's a no‑go, like, forever. Fruit belongs in its own category, dessert in its own. Blueberry muffins? Total disappointment. Lemon bars? Taste like a cleaning solution that's pretending to be sweet. Whoever invented banana splits and the "cherry on top" idea? They're basically a crime against taste. And those British chocolate oranges? Pure garbage. Strawberry milk, banana milk—pour them in the drain. Waste of time. Cheesecake? Absolute abomination. It's just cream cheese with a crust, and adding chocolate or berries only ruins it further. I'd rather skip that whole dessert. The whole trend of fruit‑lookalike pastries? Vile. Especially that shady Korean peach‑and‑lemon ice cream. I thought it'd be vanilla, but nope—total flavor sabotage. Bottom line: keep fruit separate from chocolate and creamy desserts. It's a rule, bestie. I am not going to explain why the audacity of mixing them is so wrong, because you already know the tea.
